newsitem.title: LATVIA: RTF SAYS '96 PROFIT LOW DUE RESERVES, WRITE-OFFS.
newsitem.headline: RTF SAYS '96 PROFIT LOW DUE RESERVES, WRITE-OFFS.

text.p: Riga Transport Fleet (RTF), an official list stock, said on Friday that the creation of reserves for bad debts and increased ammortisation costs were among the reasons for a low 1996 profit.
RTF earlier reported 1996 after-tax profit of 182,719 lats on turnover of 11.4 4 lats turnover and 18.27 million of basic capital. Some dealers said the RTF profit was surprisingly low.
"When (Lavinia Corporation) bought us we had bad debts and now 68 percent of the profit has been used to create a reserve fund," Antonina Burgelis, RTF's chief accountant, told a news conference.
The company also said that increased ammortisation costs were among the reasons for a low profit.
"We were bought for 16 million lats, although our statutory capital was only 3.6 million lats. According to the law, we had to revalue our assets," Burgelis said.
"Ammortisation of our ships increased by 1.5 million lats (during 1996) compared to 1995," she said.
Burgelis said that the company's books are being audited by Deloite & Touche and the work was still in progress.
